interactions_checked.interaction: Increased risk of hypoglycaemia due to additive glucose‑lowering effect
interactions_checked.action: Educate patient on hypoglycaemia symptoms; consider modest reduction of prandial insulin dose; monitor blood glucose closely after initiation

interactions_checked.interaction: Potential for modest increase in serum potassium and creatinine
interactions_checked.action: Check serum potassium and creatinine 1‑2 weeks after starting amlodipine; adjust thiazide dose if hypokalaemia occurs

contraindications.reason: Accelerate CKD progression and increase fluid retention in CKD stage 3a
contraindications.alternative: Use acetaminophen for pain; avoid OTC NSAIDs

contraindications.reason: Patient already on ACE‑I; adding an ARB would increase hyperkalaemia and AKI risk
contraindications.alternative: Do not add ARB; optimise ACE‑I dose

treatment_summary: Continue ACE‑I and thiazide for BP control, add dapagliflozin and atorvastatin per NG203 to slow CKD progression and reduce cardiovascular risk, and introduce amlodipine if BP remains above target. Monitor renal function, potassium, and glucose after initiating dapagliflozin and amlodipine. Avoid chronic NSAIDs and ACE‑I/ARB dual therapy. Address anemia after obtaining iron studies. Provide lifestyle advice on low‑salt diet, smoking cessation, and exercise.
